sum: Акции B&M подскочили в четверг до более чем годового максимума после того, как дисконтный ритейлер заявил, что его годовая прибыль может вырасти до 16%, поскольку более низкие цены и сокращение ассортимента в рамках плана восстановления помогли ему вернуть покупателей, испытывающих нехватку денежных средств.

Компания, которая продает товары, начиная от продуктов питания и предметов первой необходимости для дома до игрушек и товаров для сада, сообщила, что ее сопоставимые продажи (LFL) во втором квартале в Великобритании выросли на 3,2%, что означает восстановление после спада на 2,3% в первом квартале.
К 08:33 по Гринвичу акции B&M выросли на 19,5% до 333,4 пенсов.

Компания прогнозирует скорректированную прибыль до налогообложения в 2027 финансовом году в размере от 280 до 330 миллионов фунтов стерлингов по сравнению с консенсус-прогнозом Лондонской фондовой биржи (LSEG) в размере 290,41 миллиона фунтов стерлингов.
B&M, один из крупнейших дисконтных ритейлеров Великобритании, имеет репутацию ключевого бенефициара, когда семейные бюджеты оказываются под давлением.
Генеральный директор Тьерд Йеген, пришедший к власти в июне 2025 года, запустил свой план «Назад к основам B&M». Период с октября по декабрь был положительным во всех трех его подразделениях.
Сопоставимые продажи за шесть месяцев, закончившихся 26 сентября, выросли во Франции на 5,9%, и B&M заявила, что не увидела существенного влияния продолжающихся социальных волнений в стране.

items.t: Lloyds backs first new £500mn Plain Vanilla Bond
sum: Lloyds LON:LLOY has supported the first new issuance of a Plain Vanilla Listed Bond (PVLB), with London Stock Exchange Group LON:LSEG raising £500mn through a format designed to make corporate debt more accessible to individual investors.

The transaction marks a significant step in the development of the UK’s retail corporate bond market, moving beyond the conversion of existing debt to demonstrate how new bonds can be structured from the outset to attract both retail and institutional investors.

The LSEG bond carries a coupon of 5.50% and has a minimum denomination of £1,000, making it available to a broader pool of investors than traditional corporate bonds, which have often required substantially larger minimum investments. Lloyds acted as PVLB Coordinator, with Barclays, HSBC, NatWest and RBC Capital Markets serving as joint bookrunners.

PVLBs were introduced under the UK’s Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regime, which came into effect at the start of 2026. The framework is intended to simplify bond structures and reduce denominations, helping individual investors gain access to a wider range of corporate debt investments while giving listed companies an additional route to raise finance.
- AI exposure and company valuations: why stocks and bonds disagree

The latest issuance builds on an earlier collaboration between Lloyds and LSEG, which resulted in the UK’s first conversion of existing corporate bonds into the new format. That transaction saw £1.4bn of sterling-denominated notes converted into PVLBs, demonstrating how the framework could be applied to debt already in circulation.

The new £500mn bond takes the initiative a stage further by showing that the format can be used for fresh funding. Together, the two transactions represent important early milestones in establishing a market that could connect companies seeking capital with a wider range of investors.

Asia Pacific capital markets gather momentum as investment needs evolve
sum: - Asia Pacific excluding Japan ECM issuance reached US$302.0 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 57.2% year-on-year and its highest level in five years, with China accounting for more than half of regional proceeds.

- Technology is at the centre of the capital-raising story, but its influence extends beyond the technology sector, with some of the region’s largest transactions spanning high technology, retail and telecommunications.
- Momentum is not uniform across the region. Singapore ECM proceeds rose 28.2% year-on-year, while India declined 1.7%, illustrating the different capital-raising conditions across Asia Pacific.

Asia Pacific’s capital markets entered the final quarter of 2026 with considerable momentum. Equity and equity-linked issuance across Asia Pacific excluding Japan reached US$302.0 billion during the first nine months, rising 57.2% year-on-year to its highest level since 2021. This strength was broadly consistent with the global picture, with worldwide ECM activity reaching US$870.7 billion over the same period, up 62% year-on-year.

The quarterly picture, however, reveals a notable divergence. Global ECM activity slowed in the third quarter, with issuance falling 26% from Q2. Asia Pacific excluding Japan moved in the opposite direction, with equity and equity-related proceeds increasing 121% quarter-on-quarter. This continued regional strength came despite the number of offerings declining 2.1% over the first nine months, highlighting the role larger transactions have played in driving proceeds.

Technology provides an important lens through which to understand that strength. High Technology accounted for US$123.9 billion, or 41% of Asia Pacific excluding Japan ECM proceeds, an increase of 269.4% from the comparable period in 2025.

Among the largest transactions, SK Hynix raised US$26.5 billion through its NASDAQ ADR offering, while Alibaba completed a US$10.2 billion Hong Kong placement, the largest ever primary follow-on by a HK-listed company. CXMT also came to market with a US$9.8 billion Shanghai IPO, one of China’s largest domestic listings, while Zhongji Innolight raised US$7.8 billion through a follow-on offering.

US ESS boom lifts Korean battery makers as China faces oversupply squeeze
sum: Fortunes are diverging lately for Korean and Chinese companies competing in the global battery market. Expectations are rising that domestic manufacturers including LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI will keep improving results on stronger demand in the U.S. energy storage system (ESS) market. Chinese companies, by contrast, face a red light as oversupply worries and U.S. restrictions on Chinese-made products cloud growth.
◇ China's CATL grows in size, but profitability flashes warning signs

According to the battery industry on the 9th, China's CATL, the world's largest battery maker, posted third-quarter revenue of 165.221 billion yuan (about 33.3 trillion won), up 58.9% from a year earlier. Net profit rose 14.5% to 21.246 billion yuan (about 4.3 trillion won).

Despite double-digit increases in both revenue and net profit from a year earlier, the results fell well short of market expectations. London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) had projected CATL's third-quarter revenue growth rate at 60.2% and net profit growth rate at 41.2%, respectively.

The underwhelming results were immediately reflected in the share price. On the 20th of last month, when the third-quarter results were released, CATL's stock on the Hong Kong market fell 6.6% from the previous day. Global investment bank JPMorgan also cut its rating on CATL shares listed in Hong Kong to Neutral from Overweight.
Chinese battery makers including CATL continue to expand in scale. In particular, Chinese products have increased their share of the electric-vehicle market this year.

Market researcher SNE Research said that from January through September, Chinese companies—seven suppliers including CATL—accounted for a 73% share of batteries installed in electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) and hybrids (HEVs) worldwide, up 3.5 percentage points from a year earlier. Korea's big three—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI and SK On—had a 12.6% share, down 4.1 percentage points.

US-Iran Peace Talks Show First Glimmer as Oil Prices Plunge 17% in a Week, Worst Since Pandemic
sum: The international crude oil market underwent a sharp correction last week. As signals emerged that the United States and Iran are restarting negotiations, the market quickly unwound the geopolitical risk premium accumulated earlier because of the Middle East conflict, with Brent Crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) both posting their worst weekly declines since the COVID-19 pandemic erupted.

According to statistics from the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) dating back to 1988, Brent Crude plunged 17% last week, its biggest weekly drop since the pandemic hit global demand in 2020; WTI fell 13% over the same period. The two benchmark prices broke below the $95 and $90 thresholds respectively, with Brent's January futures crashing 9.73% in a single day on Wednesday (the 4th) to close at $93.52 a barrel, while WTI also plunged 8.88% that day to $87.56. Although prices rebounded slightly at the close on Friday (the 6th), with Brent's January futures settling at $98.32 a barrel (approx. NT$3,200) and WTI at $90.83 (approx. NT$3,000), the week's slump was already locked in.

The core drivers of this decline came from diplomacy and US politics. Democrats won both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the US midterm elections, which the market read as rising pressure on Washington to end the war with Iran, serving as the direct trigger for the oil price plunge. Third parties such as Qatar actively mediated, Iran's president revealed that the supreme leader had authorized pushing for peace talks, and both the United States and Iran signaled a return to the negotiating table. At the same time, Iran reportedly delivered a nuclear-related proposal to Washington through Qatar, giving the market hope for a de-escalation.

However, supply-side disruptions have not truly disappeared. Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported that three more tanker attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz last Thursday; security risks remain in this chokepoint carrying critical global crude shipments, and crude flows remain below 60% of normal capacity.

sum: - London Stock Exchange Group plc (LSE:LSEG) Financial Services London Stock Exchange Group PLC (LSE:LSEG) 9208.00 GBX -132.000 1.413% Last Updated at: 2026-10-27T16:35:00Z continues regular share cancellation programmes.
- LSEG is a data, analytics and markets infrastructure heavyweight.
LSEG Share Cancellation Programme filings keep capital returns in the spotlight

Under a share cancellation programme, the company uses surplus cash to acquire shares in the market and cancel them. That reduces the number in issue and can raise earnings per share over time. The disclosures show the volumes and price ranges of each daily transaction.

The company also operates clearing services through its LCH unit, which processes huge volumes of derivatives trades. Clearing income rises when markets are volatile, offering a counterweight in busy periods. Regulators view the unit as systemically important, so oversight is intense.

Most of the group's earnings now come from data and analytics, following its acquisition of a large financial data provider. Subscription-style revenue is recurring and sticky. It is complemented by trading, clearing and index businesses that benefit from busy markets.
Index and benchmark provision is another pillar, with widely used indices licensed to asset managers. These fees are recurring and tied to the growth of passive funds.

AMD Posts Record Q3 Revenue, Shares Soar After Hours
sum: U.S. semiconductor company AMD posted record quarterly revenue in the third quarter of this year, as surging demand from AI data centers drove its results. Its shares soared after the company said it expected revenue in the next quarter to exceed market forecasts.

According to CNBC, AMD reported on Nov. 3 (local time) that third-quarter revenue rose 45% year over year to $13.38 billion (about KRW 18 trillion). The revenue forecast from London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), a market research firm, was $13.09 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) also surged 74% from a year earlier to $2.09, topping the previous forecast of $1.95.

The AI data center business led the revenue growth. AMD's data center revenue in the third quarter surged 97% year over year to $8.55 billion, accounting for two-thirds of total revenue. AMD said strong sales of new graphics processing units (GPUs), including its latest AI accelerator, the Instinct MI455X, and sixth-generation EPYC central processing units (CPUs) drove the growth.

As various AI models compete to offer services, demand has grown not only for GPUs but also for CPUs, which supply data and manage workloads. This has significantly increased demand for AMD's semiconductors. Revenue from the embedded segment, whose products are used in industries such as aerospace, defense and automotive, also rose 29.4% year over year to $1.11 billion.

Data center revenue far outstripped revenue from AMD's formerly core PC semiconductor business. In the third quarter, AMD's PC semiconductor revenue rose just 7% year over year to $2.949 billion. Gaming semiconductor revenue fell 40% to $773 million. The center of AMD's growth has shifted rapidly from PCs and gaming to AI data centers.

AMD emphasized that strong results, led by its AI business, would continue in the fourth quarter. It forecast revenue of $17 billion, a 66% surge from a year earlier. That figure is well above its previous forecast of $16.2 billion.

AMD CEO Lisa Su offered an upbeat outlook on the earnings call that day, saying, "Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continues to strengthen. Growth will accelerate further in the fourth quarter." She added, "Based on the visibility we have today, we expect revenue to grow by more than 80% in 2027."

Apple posts record third-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion; shares fall 2.6% : Global : JKN
sum: Despite rising component costs and supply chain pressures, Apple recorded $114.48 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, marking its highest-ever performance for the July–September period. While growth was driven by iPhone and Mac sales, shares fell in after-hours trading due to concerns over iPhone duo supply instability and a gross margin forecast for the next quarter that failed to meet market expectations.

Apple announced on the 2nd (local time) that its revenue for the fourth quarter of the fiscal year, from July to September, reached $114.48 billion. This is a 12% increase compared to the same period last year and represents the highest revenue ever for the July–September quarter. It also surpassed the market consensus of $113.39 billion compiled by the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). Product revenue stood at $82.94 billion, while service revenue was $31.573 billion. iPhone revenue grew 17.5% year-on-year to $57.58 billion, and Mac revenue rose 23.7% to $10.79 billion. Conversely, iPad revenue fell 10.4%, and revenue for the wearables, home, and accessories segment decreased by 7.9%.

Service revenue, centered on Apple Music, Apple TV, and cloud businesses, increased by 9.8% compared to the same period last year. However, the growth rate fell to its lowest level since 2022. Diluted earnings per share (EPS) were $2.10, exceeding the market forecast of $1.99. This figure includes a $0.05 per share impact from a tax refund. As Apple previously explained that tax refunds affected its gross margin and EPS in the prior quarter, this factor was also reflected in profitability metrics in these results.

LSE Group stock: Q3 growth lifts 2026 outlook, Octus deal
sum: London Stock Exchange Group raised its 2026 outlook on October 22 after third-quarter income growth accelerated across its businesses. The company also agreed to acquire credit-data provider Octus for $3.535 billion, expanding its position in private and illiquid credit.
LSE Group stock traded at 113.73 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:29 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of London Stock Exchange Group stock.

Total income excluding recoveries reached GBP 2.407 billion in the third quarter, up 8.8% on an organic, constant-currency basis from GBP 2.219 billion a year earlier. Growth was led by Markets at 12.5%, followed by FTSE Russell at 10.2%, Risk Intelligence at 9.8% and Data & Analytics at 5.2%.

Including recoveries, total income increased to GBP 2.501 billion from GBP 2.308 billion. LSEG said subscription businesses continued to accelerate while its Markets division maintained strong momentum. The company described customer adoption of its artificial-intelligence solutions as another factor supporting the performance.

LSEG now expects organic constant-currency growth in total income excluding recoveries of at least 8.0% for 2026. That is above the 7.0% to 7.5% range given with its half-year results and would represent the group's strongest annual growth since 2018, according to management.

The company also raised its expected EBITDA margin expansion to 100 to 120 basis points and expects equity free cash flow of at least GBP 2.8 billion. The outlook gives investors a clearer measure of the operating leverage available as subscription growth and trading activity develop.

Under the agreed transaction, LSEG will buy Octus from funds advised by Permira and Octus management. Octus provides proprietary credit intelligence, data and workflows focused on private, illiquid and distressed credit. LSEG plans to combine those capabilities with its existing fixed-income data, analytics and distribution.

Financial News Celebrates South Asian Power Brokers with Closing Bell at LSEG
sum: London: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) hosted the second annual South Asian Power Brokers celebration on October 29, bringing together leaders from finance, business, and culture for a special Market Close ceremony and Diwali reception recognizing the community’s achievements and contributions.

Financial News rang the exchange’s closing bell during the ceremony. Among those attending were Deutsche Bank’s UK chief Vathany Vijayaratna, former Shell UK chair Parminder Kohli, and Cobra Beer founder Lord Karan Bilimoria.

The event followed the October 26 release of Financial News’ second annual South Asian Power Brokers list, recognizing influential leaders of South Asian heritage shaping finance and business worldwide.

Welcoming Financial News to the exchange for the second consecutive year, London Stock Exchange CEO Dame Julia Hoggett said, “It is a real joy to welcome you all here today. And can I say namaskar and welcome to the London Stock Exchange?”

Hoggett said the gathering brought together people from across business, finance, and culture to celebrate the achievements and contributions of South Asians in the City of London and the broader United Kingdom.

“At the exchange, as I’ve said, we believe in the power of convening markets and people,” she added. “Markets connect ideas with capital, businesses with investors, and ambition with opportunity. And they work best when the widest possible range of talent can contribute.”

Hoggett also highlighted the return of a bell to the exchange’s ceremonies, coinciding with the 40th anniversary of Big Bang, the 1986 reforms that transformed London’s financial markets. The bell was cast at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry, which also produced Big Ben and the original Liberty Bell.

items.t: FTSE 100 LSEG (LSE:LSEG) Rallies on Its Octus Deal
sum: - LSEG ranked among the strongest risers on a weak day for the FTSE 100.
- It agreed to buy credit-data platform Octus from Permira in an all-cash deal.
- Third-quarter total income rose compared with a year earlier.

London Stock Exchange Group (LSE:LSEG) Financial Services London Stock Exchange Group PLC (LSE:LSEG) 9208.00 GBX -132.000 1.413% Last Updated at: 2026-10-27T16:35:00Z rallied on Thursday, with the shares rising strongly on a day when the wider market was under pressure. The FTSE 100 closed lower, in a risk-off session. Banks and miners dragged the index lower, a drop in spot gold hit precious-metals miners, and a global sell-off in technology and the AI trade weighed on growth names. Higher oil prices and lingering inflation concerns were also in focus. LSEG, with its own news to digest, ran against that tide and ranked among the strongest risers on the index. Readers can follow related updates in our Financial Stocks section.

The confirmed driver was a pair of announcements. As a constituent of the FTSE 100, London Stock Exchange Group sits within the London market's most closely tracked benchmark. First, the group agreed to buy the credit-data platform Octus from Permira in an all-cash deal. Second, it reported third-quarter higher total income than a year earlier. A sizeable acquisition paid for in cash, alongside a higher income figure than a year before, gave investors a clear story to react to: the company is adding a specialist data asset while the existing business is generating more income than it did in the same quarter last year.

LSEG is an exchange operator and a financial-data and analytics provider. Its business spans trading and market infrastructure as well as information services, and it owns Refinitiv and FTSE Russell. The Octus deal fits naturally into the data and analytics side of that picture, since Octus is a credit-data platform. That description is the extent of what can be said about the target from the information available here. Details such as the strategic rationale in the companys own words, expected completion timing or financial benefits were not part of the confirmed facts, so they are not speculated on here.

"Global markets have also struggled to find momentum, held back by continued questions about the future of AI and whether the pace of its expansion needs to slow. National Stock Exchange seeks $46 bn valuation in trimmed IPO
sum: National Stock Exchange of India is seeking a valuation of up to 4.42 trillion rupees ($46.31 billion) through its long-awaited IPO, which launches next week and could rank among India's biggest-ever listings.

NSE set a price band of 1,700-1,785 rupees ($17.81-$18.70) per share for the IPO, a public filing showed early Friday. The targeted valuation, at the top of the range, would make NSE one of the country's most valuable companies and within reach of Nasdaq and London Stock Exchange Group.

India's largest bourse had on Thursday cut the size of its IPO by more than 15% as some top investors trimmed the number of shares they intended to sell, which a source told Reuters was primarily on account of a lower-than-expected price band.
The $2.36 billion IPO will likely trail an upcoming offering by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio expected to raise $3.8 billion and Hyundai Motor India's $3.3 billion issue in 2024.
The offering comes after years of delays and at a time when India's IPO market is regaining momentum after a sluggish start to the year.
NSE's share sale will open for subscription on September 17 and close on September 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for September 16. The stock is expected to list on or about September 24.
NSE, the country's biggest exchange by trading volumes, dominates the derivatives market and has benefited from a surge in retail trading in the world's most populous country.

For now, the rollout is presented as a near-term route for tokenized versions of major UK-listed shares outside the UK. Payward said the products are intended for investors in more than 110 countries, though they are not currently available to UK-based investors.

Under the announced plan, the tokens will be backed 1:1 and issued under the xStocks brand. Payward said the first products are expected to become available through Kraken and other platforms in the xStocks Alliance in the coming weeks.

The announcement covers tokenized versions of existing London-listed equities, not a new listing programme for the underlying shares, and separates their initial distribution timetable from any eventual trading on the exchange group’s new venue.

LSE 24 is planned as a Monday-to-Friday, near-continuous trading venue, operating from 17:00 to 07:50 London time with a 30-minute end-of-day processing pause. Client testing is planned by the end of 2026, subject to approvals, according to a separate LSEG announcement.

items.t: London Stock Exchange to support xStocks tokenized stock trading in Payward deal
sum: Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, is partnering with the London Stock Exchange to bring UK equities onchain. In the coming weeks Payward will issue the 100 largest London listed companies as xStocks, its tokenized equity framework. Subject to regulatory approval, the LSE then plans to list xStocks for trading on LSE 24, the 24/5 venue it announced in July. The two firms will also explore native LSE issued equity tokens.

xStocks are loan notes rather than shares. Backed Assets (JE) Limited, a Jersey company, holds the underlying stock as collateral and issues tracker certificates that replicate the share price 1:1. Holders have a claim against the issuer rather than shareholder rights, and redemptions settle in cash or crypto rather than delivery of shares. The framework has passed $40 billion in cumulative volume across more than 200,000 holders in just over a year.

Tokenizing London’s biggest names potentially extends their reach to investors in more than 110 countries rather than changing anything for domestic holders who don’t currently have access. Payward pitches this to issuers as a new global channel for their shares.

The stocks that xStocks represent are also increasingly global, with Payward noting that xStocks will track US, EU, UK, Hong Kong, alongside additional asset classes. In July Payward partnered with Dubai’s GTN to tokenize international stocks, starting with those in Hong Kong. It also has a tie up with Deutsche Börse’s Clearstream. So LSE becomes an overnight trading venue for tokenized exposure to stocks listed on NYSE, Nasdaq, Deutsche Börse and HKEX, none of whom are party to the venue.

sum: London stocks were still lower by midday on Thursday as concerns about sticky US inflation overshadowed strong quarterly earnings from US chip maker Nvidia, and as investors eyed a hotly-anticipated speech by new Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh.
The FTSE 100 was down 0.5% at 10,826.20, while Brent crude was up 0.8% at $88.50 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate was 0.2% higher at $82.40.

Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said: "The Footsie may have flirted with fresh closing highs yesterday, but sentiment looks set to become more cautious as investors refocus on worries about inflation proving sticky, huge government debt piles and the prospect of interest rates lingering at elevated levels. The key central bankers’ meeting at Jackson Hole is getting underway, and Fed chair Kevin Warsh’s speech tomorrow will be closely watched for hints about the future path of interest rates.

"While headline inflation has dipped back, it’s not such a benign picture if you look at the Fed’s preferred measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index. It captures a broader range of prices and spending behaviour, and it’s still running hot - headline PCE is at 3.7%, while core PCE came in at 3.3%, above forecasts. That leaves the Fed with a tricky balancing act, with inflation still well above its 2% target just as signs of a cooling economy and a weakening jobs market come to the fore.

"There is some relief on the energy front, however, with Brent crude falling back again to $87 a barrel. Hopes are growing that a framework being worked on by Iran and Oman could pave the way for safer shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, easing fears of prolonged disruption to global oil supplies. That is taking some of the geopolitical risk premium out of the price of crude, although the waterway is not yet fully reopened and the wider conflict remains far from resolved, so the risk of renewed volatility remains."

Investors were also mulling the latest earnings from Nvidia, whose shares were set to rally on Thursday after it reported a doubling of revenues in the second quarter and delivered sales guidance well ahead of market forecasts.

sum: On Thursday, Microsoft announced a new operating business called Microsoft Frontier Company, focused on delivering successful enterprise AI deployments with Microsoft’s existing AI tools. The project will be backed by a $2.5 billion investment from Microsoft, as well as 6,000 industry and engineering experts.

In a statement announcing the venture, Microsoft’s Commercial Business CEO Judson Althoff resisted the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) label that is often applied to these ventures. “This goes beyond what has been labeled as Forward-Deployed Engineering,” Althoff wrote, “and will be the largest, most capable, outcome-driven engineering organization in the industry.”

Nonetheless, the venture bears a striking similarity to a number of FDE-based AI ventures announced in recent months. Just two days earlier, Amazon Web Services announced an internal commitment of $1 billion for its own AI deployment venture, explicitly embracing the FDE model. Both OpenAI and Anthropic have launched joint ventures along similar lines, although those efforts also involve outside capital from private equity firms.

Microsoft’s existing client base will give the new effort a significant head start, as the company has already deployed engineers to much of the Fortune 500. The announcement cites an early partnership with the London Stock Exchange Group, as well as Unilever, Land O’Lakes, and Accenture.

sum: Stocks with above-average dividend yields often represent mature businesses with resilient earnings and disciplined management. These are precisely the types of investments that can provide an anchor of stability in volatile market conditions.

However, advisers who simply chase the highest dividend yields risk exposing their clients to capital losses and income disruption. Abnormally high yields, often called “yield traps”, can be a precursor to dividend cuts: traders usually anticipate such cuts by marking down share prices, and dividend yields are calculated using backward-looking data.

A more strategic high-income equity solution can capture the benefits of dividend stocks while avoiding the pitfalls of overly simplistic approaches. To meet growing investor interest in these smarter strategies, FTSE Russell launched the FTSE Global Equity High Income Index Series in May 2024.

The index series uses a simple, capitalisation-weighted methodology to reflect the performance of global stocks with relatively high tax-adjusted dividend yields, while also addressing concerns about potential yield traps.
Six steps to the FTSE Global Equity High Income Index Series

High-dividend indices vary in the complexity of their construction methodologies. For this index series, we have adopted a simple rank-and-select rule to choose constituents. The index series follows six intuitive design steps:

Use forward-looking dividend statements. We use forecast dividends rather than trailing, or historic, dividends to rank potential index constituents. Although there is close alignment between the two measures, and past dividends are often a reliable indicator of future payments, forecast dividends cover almost all global equity markets and are more responsive to changes in market conditions.

sum: Shares in London Stock Exchange Group Plc (LSE:LSEG) fell more than 4% after Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded the stock to "neutral" from a more positive stance and reduced its price target to £104 from £120.

The broker cited concerns that advances in artificial intelligence could increase pressure on parts of LSEG's Data & Analytics business, particularly areas exposed to changing customer behaviour and evolving methods of data consumption.

In its research note, Redburn described LSEG's earnings profile as becoming "increasingly bar-belled," arguing that some of the group's businesses remain highly resilient while others face growing structural challenges.
According to the broker, operations such as real-time market data, index services and post-trade infrastructure continue to benefit from strong competitive positions and high barriers to entry.
However, it warned that products linked to workflow tools, terminals and segments of non-real-time data services may be more vulnerable to technological disruption.
"These concerns are not without merit," Redburn said, adding that a shift toward "modular, API- and AI-driven data consumption may prove structurally deflationary for parts of the model."

The broker estimated that approximately 30% of LSEG's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation could face downside risk under what it described as a realistic base-case scenario.

Dotlines was first established as a developer of bespoke B2B software in Malaysia in 2007 and has since evolved into a UK-headquartered international technology group with proprietary technology platforms and solutions. It operates in the telecommunications, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and financial technology sectors where demand is being driven by increased digitalisation, higher data usage and a growing focus on security and resilience.
Dotlines is experiencing strategic and commercial momentum across its two principal divisions:

- Sohoj Platform, a digital lifestyle platform for migrant populations in Malaysia and the principal operating vertical of the Dotlines’ digital content and services division, has served over a million migrants from countries across Asia. In 2025, it began developing a non-diaspora customer segment through a third-party partnership with Touch ’n Go, the most popular mobile wallet provider in Malaysia.

- Since July 2025, both its Catena telecoms software platform and Audra cybersecurity products and services have been successfully launched into the UK market alongside Carnival Internet, Dotlines’ UK-based full fibre broadband service.

Dotlines’ admission to AIM follows its reverse takeover by Ikigai Ventures for a total consideration of £55.7 million. Based on the issue price of 9.5p per share, the market capitalisation of Dotlines was c. £57.9 million on admission.

“Today marks an important milestone for Dotlines as we begin our life on AIM. Having commenced our journey in Malaysia almost 20 years ago, we are now operating in the UK under three brands and we believe our listing on AIM will provide a strong platform to facilitate our growth in the UK and internationally. This is a very proud moment for Dotlines and we look forward to delivering on our strategy and generating value for our shareholders.”

FTSE Russell introduces benchmarks for new Asia Pacific government bond futures on Singapore Exchange (SGX)
sum: The Asia Pacific region’s local currency government bond markets are large and increasingly integrated into global portfolios. For many investors, however, access and risk management tools remain fragmented across countries, tenors and market structures. Different trading conventions, varying liquidity conditions and operational complexity can make it challenging to express sovereign duration views or to manage exposure efficiently across the region.

FTSE Russell has developed the FTSE Asia Pacific liquid government bond index series in response to these market dynamics. The series is built on a transparent, rules-based framework and focuses on liquid segments of sovereign yield curves across five key Asia Pacific bond markets. The benchmarks also serve as the underlying references for new futures contracts listed on the Singapore Exchange, illustrating how robust index design can support the continued development of the Asia Pacific region’s fixed income market infrastructure.

The FTSE Asia Pacific Liquid Government Bond Index Series—covering India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines across three key tenors (three-, five- and ten‑year)—now serves as the underlying benchmark for the new futures contracts. (see Figure 1).

Each contract provides exposure to a clearly defined country/tenor “sector group,” constructed from a small basket of the most recently issued or reopened government bonds. By capturing liquidity across two or three benchmark bonds rather than relying on a single issue, the structure supports more stable exposure.

sum: Never miss an important update on your stock portfolio and cut through the noise. Over 7 million investors trust Simply Wall St to stay informed where it matters for FREE.

LSEG shares jump 5% after exchange group triples buyback to £3 billion
sum: London Stock Exchange Group responds to activist pressure with one of the highest shareholder yields in the UK market

Shares in London Stock Exchange Group PLC (LSE:LSEG), the financial data and markets infrastructure company, rose 5% to 8,160p after it tripled its share buyback programme to £3 billion over the next 12 months, up from £1 billion previously.
The enlarged buyback gives LSEG a buyback yield of 7.7% on top of an indicated dividend yield of 2%, making it one of the highest-yielding stocks in the UK market.
Annual results for 2025 were broadly in line with consensus, while guidance for EBITDA margin expansion of 80 to 100 basis points this year came in above expectations.
The company also issued new medium-term targets for 2027 to 2029, forecasting a cumulative 150 basis points of EBITDA margin improvement and mid to high single-digit organic revenue growth.

Analysts at Panmure Liberum said LSEG had "clearly listened" to Elliott Advisers, the activist investor that recently built a stake in the company, noting the buyback should significantly lift the share price.
However, the broker cautioned the programme is not sustainable over the long term and does not address LSEG's high debt load.

GlobalData shares rise as firm confirms move to London Main Market
sum: Industry intelligence provider to delist from AIM in March and join Official List via introduction
GlobalData PLC (AIM:DATA) shares rose 2% to 97.2p after the company confirmed plans to transfer its listing from AIM to the London Stock Exchange's Main Market on 5 March 2026.

The information services group said it will apply for admission of its entire issued ordinary share capital to the Equity Shares (Commercial Companies) segment of the Financial Conduct Authority's Official List.
The move will be executed by way of an introduction, with no new shares issued.
The final day of trading on AIM is expected to be 4 March, with the transfer completing at 8.00am. the following day.
Admission remains subject to regulatory approvals, including the publication of a prospectus and acceptance by both the Financial Conduct Authority and the London Stock Exchange.
The company's admission to AIM will be cancelled concurrently with its entry onto the Main Market. The move does not require shareholder approval.

Is it safe to buy the dip as the LSEG share price implodes?
sum: The LSEG share price is in a steep freefall as concerns about its business continue. London Stock Exchange stock tumbled to a low of 7,180p, its lowest level since March 2023. It has dropped by over 40% from its highest point in February 2025.
The London Stock Exchange stock price has crashed in the past few months, moving from a high of 12,025p to a low of 7,200p.

There are two primary reasons why the stock has been in a strong downward trend this year. First, there are concerns that a major part of its business will be disrupted by the fast-growing artificial intelligence tools, especially those made by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI.

The main concern is that these AI companies have come up with tools that may disrupt some of its businesses. That’s because, while the London Stock Exchange is known for running the biggest exchange in London, its most important business is in the data industry.

Anthropic, the creator of Claude, unveiled a new tool allowing customers to simplify the legal industry. The plugin can help companies speed up the legal process by automating NDA triage, contract review, and compliance workflows.
While Anthropic’s plugin may disrupt the industry, we believe that it will be a companion to LSEG’s solutions. This means that clients will likely not end their contracts with LSEG.

LSEG share price has also crashed because of the ongoing IPO drought in London. There have been no major IPOs in the past few months. Still, on the positive side, some companies like Monzo, Revolut, and Starling Bank may opt to go public this year. Some, however, may opt to list in the United States.

items.t: Introducing the Culture Podcast: Conversations That Matter
sum: We’re thrilled to introduce Culture Conversations, our new podcast and video series exploring the intersection of culture, leadership and high performance.

Launching Monday 2 February, we’re joined by David Schwimmer, LSEG CEO, for our first episode, where the three of us engage in an in‑depth conversation about the cultural transformation shaping LSEG. Together, we reflect on the bold decisions, cultural shifts and long‑term vision driving the transformation of LSEG, a global leader in financial markets, data and analytics.

This podcast is born out of a shared belief: that culture isn’t a buzzword — it’s the heartbeat of high‑performing organisations. As leaders, we’ve seen how inclusive, values‑driven environments unlock creativity, resilience and long‑term success. But we also know that culture is intentional. It’s shaped by the choices we make, the stories we tell and the behaviours we reward.

In each episode, we speak to trailblazers across industries — from CEOs and creatives to changemakers and culture builders — who are redefining what leadership looks like in today’s world. Upcoming guests include:
- Sung‑Joo Kim, Founder and CEO of Sungjoo Group and Chairperson and CEO of MCM Worldwide

Together, we’re unpacking the habits, mindsets and pivotal moments that shape high‑performance cultures. We’re asking the hard questions, sharing honest reflections and spotlighting the voices and visionaries driving meaningful change.

Why are we doing this? Because we believe culture is the most powerful lever for transformation. We believe in championing bold disruptors who are willing to challenge the status quo, and we’ve seen that performance thrives when people feel connected to something bigger than themselves. That’s why this work matters to us.

items.t: Why screening sanctioned securities matters
sum: Sanctions compliance is no longer just about screening names. As global regulations evolve, firms must identify risks tied to ownership, control and even securities linked to sanctioned entities.
- Sanctions screening has evolved beyond basic name matching – firms must now identify risks linked to ownership, control, and associated entities to meet regulatory expectations.
- Automated screening is essential – with frequent regulatory updates and complex ownership structures, technology-driven solutions enable timely, accurate, and scalable compliance.
- From entities to instruments: closing the gap in sanctions screening – join global webinar to learn more.

For many years, the screening against sanctions was straightforward, as the regulatory expectation was that financial institutions only needed to perform checks against set lists of people and entities based on names and, where possible, secondary identifiers.

That reality started to change with the introduction of implicit sanctions screening requirements, such as the “OFAC 50% rule”. The message behind this type of regulation? Since attempts at circumventing restrictions move faster than the legislation itself, screening against a pre-defined list was no longer good enough. So, expectations were expanded to account for the screening of entities owned or controlled by sanctioned subjects.

The next step of this evolution went beyond the concept of companies, and into another form of ownership: financial instruments. The goal of monetary sanctions is to prevent blacklisted parties from accessing or moving funds. As a result, securities such as bonds and shares became a key screening target. This shift introduced an extra layer of complexity in managing financial portfolios, making it critical for institutions to identify and manage exposure to restricted securities.
